name: Nora Nolasco
life: “I still remember my own name becoming illegible in a school register.” On Tuesday, near the market by Market Flats, Nora often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I brought a petition and the names ran together. My opponents helped me remember who had signed.
appearance: Nora has auburn hair cut square at the nape, a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, and a favorite piece of clothing, an unlined tan jacket. It usually goes with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. When somebody else has the floor, Nora squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Nora finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To reconstruct the names with both sides present.
family: Ivy Knight is Nora’s second cousin. Nora chooses whether to use it. Ivy saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The upstairs piano*, Ivy says, “I'm deaf in one ear. The landing is the only place in this building where I hear the bass clearly.”
connections: Lucia Webb. The petitions reach signers in more than one language. Also in the story is Cecilia Aranda (station host).
